execution_batches.description: Restore the phase-2 runtime shape by putting operational orchestration back between the FIFO queue and business execution.
Add operational state control and duplicate protection across domain contracts and persistence boundaries.
Align infrastructure, remove phase-1 leftovers, and validate the full resilient flow.

tasks.title: Reintroduce orchestrator-driven runtime between SQS and provider execution
outputs: One explicit phase-2 runtime path from FIFO queue into operational orchestration
exit_criteria: The queue no longer represents the direct runtime trigger for business execution.
The orchestrator consumes SQS messages and starts one operational execution per valid work item.
Invalid queue payloads are surfaced as batch failures instead of being silently ignored.

tasks.title: Reintroduce business consumer entrypoint for Step Functions invocation
outputs: One consumer entrypoint dedicated to provider execution inside the orchestration flow
exit_criteria: The consumer receives one ProviderRecord from Step Functions.
Successful provider results are persisted by the consumer.
Terminal provider failures are persisted by the consumer and exposed as terminal control flow.
Transient failures are propagated for orchestration-level retry handling.

tasks.title: Add idempotency contracts and duplicate-protection persistence
outputs: Dedicated idempotency model and persistence path for duplicate blocking
exit_criteria: A canonical idempotency key is defined as recordId plus scheduledDate.
Duplicate work items cannot produce a second independent execution.
Idempotency state supports IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, and FAILED closure paths.
Idempotency persistence remains separate from pending and results tables.

tasks.title: Add pending-record lifecycle transitions and final exhausted-failure closure
outputs: Operational lifecycle visibility on pending records and final closure for all end states
exit_criteria: Pending records transition from PENDING to IN_PROGRESS when work begins.
Pending records transition to COMPLETED on successful closure.
Pending records transition to FAILED on terminal or exhausted retry closure.
Exhausted transient failures are persisted as final failed business outcomes.

tasks.title: Align CDK infrastructure with the resilient phase-2 architecture
outputs: Infrastructure definition matching the queue to orchestrator to Step Functions to consumer runtime
exit_criteria: The stack provisions orchestrator Lambda, Step Functions, and the idempotency table.
SQS points to the orchestrator instead of directly to the business consumer.
Step Functions permissions cover pending-state updates, idempotency closure, and exhausted-failure persistence.
The stack continues preserving FIFO queue behavior and DLQ safety net.

tasks.title: Remove phase-1-only runtime leftovers and keep the codebase coherent
outputs: A repo without obsolete runtime entrypoints or tests from the simplified phase-1 flow
exit_criteria: Phase-1-only runtime leftovers do not remain in the active code path.
There is no ambiguity about which handlers are operationally active in phase 2.
Tests and references no longer rely on obsolete queue-to-consumer direct flow.

tasks.title: Validate resilient behavior in code and deployment-facing checks
outputs: Passing local quality gates and an operational validation plan for AWS
exit_criteria: Build passes.
Unit tests cover producer, consumer, and orchestrator behavior under the phase-2 runtime.
CDK synth succeeds for the resilient architecture.
The validation plan covers success, terminal failure, exhausted transient retry, and duplicate blocking.
